predecessors.name: Kingdom of Zimbabwe
predecessors.text: 'some Karanga from Great Zimbabwe migrated slowly to the northern Zimbabwean Plateau'

successors.name: Portuguese Mozambique
successors.text: the Chidima region of Mozambique, drawn as Tete province without the territory around Tete returned to the Portuguese in 1629

capitals.name: Chidima region (Zambezi Valley, Mozambique; stand-in: Luangwa, Tete province)

ledger.x: c. 1430: the Mutapa state is founded on the northern Zimbabwean Plateau by Nyatsimba Mutota, who leaves Great Zimbabwe. The page gives only 'Established: 15th century' and says Mutota is the founder only 'according to tradition'; the year is a bridge. [Repair 2026-10-19: the Nyatsimba Mutota page gives the infobox…

c. 1450: Matope conquers 'all Tavara and Tonga from the Musengezi River eastwards to the Ruenya River'. The page does not date the conquest, so the year is a bridge between the founding and the 1490 revolt.
c. 1470: Nyahuma Mukombero 'expanded to conquer Uteve', and Barue under his vassal Makombe sends Chikanga to occupy Manyika. The page does not date either; the year is a bridge.

c. 1607: Barue and Manyika break away. 'by 1607 Gatsi had lost control of his zimbabwe and the empire'; 'Gatsi next tried to reconquer Barue which had refused to pay tribute'; 'Manyika also broke free at this time.' [Repair 2026-10-19: the Kingdom of Barue page puts the break at 1608: 'In 1608, Barue ceased paying…
c. 1607: Manyika 'broke free at this time'; the Portuguese later 'conquered Manyika' (1632).
1629: after defeat at Masapa the Mwenemutapa Mavhura signs terms of vassalage with the Portuguese Crown, including 'the return of territory around Tete that Gatsi Rusere had conquered'.
c. 1663: under Mukombwe (reign c. 1663-1692) 'both Barue and Manyika accepted his suzerainty'.

c. 1692: Mukombwe's reign ends; the page does not say when Barue's suzerainty lapsed, and after Changamire Dombo's war in the 1690s 'all Portuguese feiras were abandoned save for ones in Manyika'. [Repair 2026-10-19: the Kingdom of Barue page does not mention Mukombwe or any end of suzerainty; it dates the break to…
c. 1692: end of Mukombwe's reign; Manyika's tie to Mutapa is not dated further.
1690s: 'the Rozvi Empire took control of the remaining gold-producing regions' of Mutapa after Changamire Dombo's forces attacked Dambarare in 1693 and 'invaded Manyika' in 1695.
1723: 'From 1723 onwards the capital was located in the Zambezi Valley rather than on the Plateau' (the Chidima region of Mozambique in the 18th century).
c. 1760: after Mupunzagutu is killed by his brother Zindove 'the state is said to have disintegrated into principalities'; 'Dande did split away from the state'.
1885: 'In 1884 the Portuguese attacked Mutapa and curtailed Dzuda's power, annexing Chidima a year later and forcing Dzuda into exile.'
1885: the Mutapa state is annexed by Portugal and Dzuda goes into exile (infobox: 'Conquered by the Portuguese: 1884').

wars.name: Changamire's revolt and the Mutapa-Butua wars
wars.outcome: c. 1490 Changamire 'led an army to Mukombwe's zimbabwe and killed him'; around 1494 Chikuyo returned 'with a large army'; the Mwenemutapa fought Changamire II 'until at least 1512'. No border change is dated.

wars.name: Mutapa-Teve wars
wars.outcome: 'Little is known about the Mutapa-Teve wars, except that they were reignited during the early 1540s'; Nyamunda began campaigns 'c.

wars.name: Mutapa-Portuguese war and the 1629 vassalage
wars.outcome: 1629: Kapararidze's forces met the Portuguese army at Masapa and Mavhura signed terms of vassalage; 1631 Kapararidze routed the Mavhura-Portuguese army; 1632 a Portuguese captain 'led an army to subdue the Valley from Quelimane to Sena, and conquered Manyika'.

wars.name: Changamire Dombo's wars against Mutapa and the Portuguese
wars.outcome: 'Around 1683, Dombo's forces attacked the Portuguese forces of the Governor of Mozambique in Maungwe'; 1693 the feira of Dambarare; 1695 Manyika; Dombo died c.

certainty.note: Plateau and valley tributary realm with no boundaries described; infobox area is flagged dubious by the page.
The 1629 terms return the territory around Tete, but the page draws no line; the 1884-85 annexation is the first dated cession.
